name: Spectrality of the adic spectrum

name: Rational opens are affinoid

name: The MacWilliams identity

name: The Construction A lattice

name: Cellular equals singular homology

name: Euler–Poincaré

name: The homology of spheres

name: The prime ideal theorem
about: for every number field, `ψ_K(x) ~ x`, `ϑ_K(x) ~ x` and `π_K(x) ~ Li(x)`, with no hypotheses left to supply.

name: The Wiener–Ikehara theorem
about: suppose nonnegative coefficients have a Dirichlet series `F` on `Re s > 1`, and `F(s) - κ/(s-1)` extends continuously to `Re s ≥ 1`. Then `x⁻¹ ∑_{n≤x} a n → κ`. Variants cover natural cutoffs, a positive abscissa, and coefficients in a finite-dimensional ordered vector space.

name: Prime-number-theorem transfer
about: boundary data with residue `δ` for the von Mangoldt series of a prime set gives `ψ ~ δx`, `ϑ ~ δx` and `π ~ δ Li(x)`.

name: Nonvanishing on the line `Re s = 1`
about: `ζ_K` has no zeros there away from its pole, by the 3-4-1 argument. The same argument covers the continued L-function of a unitary weight whose pointwise square also has cancellation.

about: a von Mangoldt series together with a continuous boundary remainder and a residue. Every prime-counting consumer supplies this package, and the transfer theorem consumes it. The instance for all primes now lives in an `LFunctions` file.

name: The continued L-function of a weight
about: it is defined by partial summation and agrees with the `L`-series on `Re s > 1`. When the weight has cancellation it is holomorphic on `Re s > 1 - 1/[K:ℚ]`. This is what lets character-family consumers leave the half-plane of convergence.

name: One-sided Dirichlet-density bounds
about: the epsilon inequalities that squeeze arguments use; matching bounds force a density. Natural density has a parallel calculus: finite and density-zero changes, readings against `Li(x)` and `x / log x`, and fibre counts along contraction.

name: Freeness of the fundamental group of the thrice-punctured sphere
about: `π₁(ℂ ∖ {0, 1}, 1/2)` is free of rank two, with the peripheral loops around `0` and `1` as basis.

name: Covers are classified by their triples
about: connected degree-`n` covers of `ℂ ∖ {0, 1}` up to isomorphism correspond bijectively to isomorphism classes of connected degree-`n` triples. about: on the standard grid of the `(p+1, q+1)` torus knot, 2τ = −pq, so `τ = −3` on the `T(3,4)` grid. This is the acceptance check `τ(T_{3,4}) = 3` up to an orientation sign that has not been reconciled, and it is still a statement about one grid.

name: The Euler characteristic of grid homology

name: The `U`-tower in lattice homology
about: in every negative-definite plumbing, a minimal-weight lattice point gives a cycle no nonzero multiple of which is a boundary.

name: The Riemann mapping theorem
about: every nonempty, simply connected, proper open subset of `ℂ` admits a holomorphic bijection onto the unit disc, with normalized and uniqueness forms.

name: Carathéodory's boundary correspondence

name: The Schwarz–Christoffel theorem

name: Finite-order Hecke characters are ray class characters

name: The quaternary case of Hasse–Minkowski

name: The Hasse–Minkowski induction step in rank at least five

name: Quaternary descent
about: a regular quaternary form whose plain discriminant is the class of a nonsquare `d` is isotropic over `F` exactly when it is isotropic over `F(√d)` (O'Meara 58:7).

name: Local equivalence by invariants
about: two regular forms are isometric at every finite and real place exactly when their ranks, their discriminants at every finite place, their finite Hasse signs and their real positive indices agree.

name: Uniqueness of projective resolutions

name: The Gaussian `W₂` formula
about: from a nondegenerate Gaussian to any Gaussian, `W₂²` is the squared distance of the means plus the Bures covariance term, realised by the positive affine map.

name: Existence and uniqueness of the Schrödinger minimiser
about: against a finite reference measure, a finite static Schrödinger value is attained by exactly one coupling, with no topology on the spaces.

name: The peripheral product identity
about: for every unit `u` there are conjugators, the first one trivial, such that the conjugated `u`-th powers of the basis and of the cusp multiply to `1` in order. name: The peripheral-power theorem
about: for every unit `u`, some continuous automorphism of a free pro-`p` group of finite rank sends each basis element and the cusp to a conjugate of its `u`-th power, and fixes the first basis element's power exactly. name: Sₙ is a Galois group over ℚ
about: for every n ≥ 1 there is a monic integral polynomial of degree n that is irreducible over ℚ and has the full symmetric group as its Galois group. This is van der Waerden's construction from reductions at 2, 3 and 5.

name: The transitive subgroups of S₅
about: every transitive subgroup of S₅ is conjugate to exactly one of C₅, D₅, F₂₀, A₅ and S₅, and the same holds in degrees three and four.

name: The factorization theorem for resolvents
about: when a specialized resolvent is separable, its irreducible factors correspond to the orbits of the Galois image on Sₙ/H, and their degrees are the orbit sizes.

name: Resolvents through a Tschirnhaus transform
about: if T is admissible for f and the transformed resolvent is separable with a root in the base field, then the Galois image of f lies in a conjugate of H. This is the classical remedy for a degenerate resolvent.

name: The quintic solvability criterion
about: an irreducible separable quintic has a solvable Galois group exactly when its separable F₂₀ resolvent sextic has a root in the base field. The sextic and the discriminant together still cannot separate C₅ from D₅, and that limitation is proved with explicit witnesses.

name: Resolvent specifications
about: an integral invariant whose stabilizer is exactly H, together with its orbit product written in the elementary symmetric polynomials. It can be specialized at any polynomial over any ring, so one universal object serves every polynomial, every field and every reduction mod p.

name: Galois labels
about: a polynomial has label `nTj` when some numbering of its roots carries its Galois image onto a conjugate of the reference subgroup. about: for a pro-`p` group `G`, the continuous automorphisms acting trivially on the Frattini quotient [form a pro-`p` group](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/ContinuousAut/ProP.html#TauCeti.IsProP.isProP_ker_mapQuotient_proPFrattini), which is open when `G` is topologically finitely generated, so `ContinuousAut G` is virtually pro-`p`.

name: The degree-one basis of a free pro-`p` group
about: for the free pro-`p` group on finitely many generators, the brackets `[x̄_i, x̄_j]`, `i < j`, form a `ℤ_p`-basis of `gr_1` of the closed lower central series.

name: The profinite power

name: Riemann forms are polarizations
about: for a complex structure J on the realification of a flat lattice, the Riemann forms of J are exactly the forms that polarize its effective weight-one Hodge structure. This is the abelian-variety case of the theory.

name: Self-duality of polarized structures

name: Moment determinacy
about: a finite measure on `ℝ` with a single finite exponential moment is determined by its polynomial moments. This is the one completeness mechanism behind every basis here, proved through characteristic functions and strip-analyticity rather than the roadmap's entire Fourier integral.

about: every pointed connected cover of `(X, x₀)` is isomorphic over `X` to `UniversalCover x₀ / H` for exactly one subgroup `H`, with conjugacy classes for unpointed covers and normal subgroups for regular ones.

name: The monodromy equivalence
about: monodromy is an equivalence from covering spaces of `X` to functors from the fundamental groupoid to types, and over a path-connected base to `π₁(X, x₀)`-sets.

name: The fundamental group as fibre-functor automorphisms
